gloss: Searching for a horse based on a drawing; following a plan too rigidly.
teaser: Ever wondered how a picture can mislead you in your search for success?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how a picture can mislead you in your search for success? [break 1s] The phrase is: 按图索骥, àn tú suǒ jì. [break 0.5s] 按 (àn) - to press or to follow [break 0.5s] 图 (tú) - picture or drawing [break 0.5s] 索 (suǒ) - to search or look for [break 0.5s] 骥 (jì) - steed or horse [break 1s] So, 按图索骥 literally means 'to search for a horse based on a drawing.' Figuratively, it refers to following a plan too rigidly or being overly reliant on a guideline. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom comes from the tale of a prince who wanted to find a famous horse. A painter drew a picture of this horse, and the prince sent out his men to find it. However, they only looked for horses that matched the drawing, ignoring other qualities of a good horse. This led them to miss out on many excellent horses that didn’t look exactly like the one in the picture. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他按图索骥，没有看到其他更好的选择。 [break 1s] He searched for a horse based on the drawing and missed out on better options. [break 1s] Example 2: 在工作中，不能只按图索骥，要灵活应变。 [break 1s] In work, you can’t just follow the plan rigidly; you need to be adaptable. [break 1s] Example 3: 学习时，不要按图索骥，要理解概念。 [break 1s] When studying, don’t just follow the guide; understand the concepts. [break 1s] So, 按图索骥 means to search for something based on a rigid guideline. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
